Activation functions

Source: R/nn.R
nn_activations.Rd

Ports of the jax.nn activation functions. All are elementwise except nn_glu, which splits x in two halves along axis (0-based). nn_relu, nn_relu6 and nn_log1mexp have custom JVP rules as in JAX: the derivative of nn_relu at 0 is 0, and the derivative of nn_relu6 is 0 at 0 and at 6. nn_swish is an alias of nn_silu, nn_hard_swish of nn_hard_silu and nn_tanh of jnp_tanh().

Usage

nn_identity(x)

nn_relu(x)

nn_squareplus(x, b = 4L)

nn_softplus(x)

nn_sparse_plus(x)

nn_soft_sign(x)

nn_sigmoid(x)

nn_sparse_sigmoid(x)

nn_silu(x)

nn_swish(x)

nn_mish(x)

nn_log_sigmoid(x)

nn_elu(x, alpha = 1)

nn_leaky_relu(x, negative_slope = 0.01)

nn_hard_tanh(x)

nn_celu(x, alpha = 1)

nn_selu(x)

nn_gelu(x, approximate = TRUE)

nn_glu(x, axis = -1L)

nn_relu6(x)

nn_hard_sigmoid(x)

nn_hard_silu(x)

nn_hard_swish(x)

nn_log1mexp(x)

nn_tanh(x)

Arguments

x

Input array.

b

Smoothness parameter of nn_squareplus.

alpha

Scalar or array of alpha values (nn_elu, nn_celu).

negative_slope

Slope for negative inputs of nn_leaky_relu.

approximate

Use the tanh approximation of nn_gelu (default) or the exact formulation with erfc.

axis

0-based axis along which nn_glu splits its input.

Value

An array.

Details

Arguments are not promoted to floating point unless JAX does so: nn_relu of an int32 array is int32, while nn_relu6 and nn_gelu return floating point arrays.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- jnp_array(c(-2, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2))
nn_relu(x)
nn_gelu(x, approximate = FALSE)
grad(function(v) nn_relu(v))(0)
} # }
